title: Word Problems with Two-Step Equations
short: Write and solve an equation, then compare with an arithmetic solution.

blocks.html: Word problems turn into the equations you can already solve: two-step equations and equations with parentheses. The new skill is writing the equation.
Name the unknown with a letter. Write the story as an equation, one piece at a time. Solve it, then check the answer in the story, not only in the equation.

An equation records what happens in the story, in order. Solving it undoes those steps in reverse. That is exactly what you would do with arithmetic: "take away the fee, then share by the price." The equation and the arithmetic are the same thinking written two ways.

blocks.name: tapediagram

steps: 4 people each spend x + 3, and the total is 56: 4(x + 3) = 56.

blocks.cap: Four friends each buy a ticket ($x$) and a \$3 snack, \$56 in all.

blocks.title: A fee plus a price per visit
blocks.q: A climbing gym charges a \$15 fee plus \$8 per visit. Lena has paid \$63. How many visits is that?
steps: Let $v$ be the number of visits: $8v + 15 = 63$.
Arithmetic check: $63 - 15 = 48$ dollars were for visits, and $48 \div 8 = 6$ ✓.

blocks.title: Equal groups
blocks.q: Four friends each buy a ticket and a \$3 snack. Together they spend \$56. How much is one ticket?
steps: Check in the story: each spends $11 + 3 = 14$, and $4 \times 14 = 56$ ✓.

blocks.title: Perimeter
blocks.q: A rectangle is 14 cm long and its perimeter is 46 cm. How wide is it?

blocks.html: Watch for amounts that happen once (a fee) and amounts that happen for each one (a price per visit). The ones that repeat get multiplied by the unknown.
